key_concept_tested: too many tools degrade selection reliability
stem: Your customer support agent has access to 15 different MCP tools including get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human, plus various analytics and reporting tools. What is the primary risk of this configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: The agent will consume too much compute processing all tool descriptions

options.label: B
options.text: Tool execution latency will increase linearly with the number of available tools

options.label: C
options.text: Claude's tool selection reliability degrades when presented with too many options

options.label: D
options.text: The MCP protocol has a hard limit of 10 tools per agent instance

explanation: Research shows that large language models exhibit decreased selection accuracy when presented with many tool options, similar to choice overload in human decision-making. The other options are incorrect - compute overhead is minimal, latency isn't directly correlated with tool count, and MCP has no hard tool limits.

stem: In your multi-agent research system, the web search subagent is incorrectly calling document_analysis tools instead of focusing on search. The coordinator shows 23% task completion delays. What should you implement?

options.label: A
options.text: Add explicit prompt instructions telling the search agent not to use analysis tools

options.label: B
options.text: Implement tool access scoping so each subagent only receives tools relevant to its specialization

options.label: C
options.text: Use tool_choice: 'any' to let the model freely select from all available tools

options.label: D
options.text: Restrict the search subagent's allowedTools to only include web_search and related tools

explanation: Restricting allowedTools to only include relevant tools prevents the agent from accessing out-of-specialization tools entirely. Prompt-only restrictions are unreliable, tool_choice: 'any' would worsen the problem, and 'tool access scoping' is vague compared to the concrete allowedTools configuration.

stem: A colleague suggests giving all customer support subagents access to the full tool suite (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human, generate_analytics_report, sync_crm_data) to 'maximize flexibility.' What is the primary flaw in this approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Subagents will frequently select inappropriate tools outside their specialization, reducing overall system reliability

options.label: B
options.text: The MCP server will become overloaded handling requests from multiple agents simultaneously

options.label: C
options.text: Tool execution costs will increase exponentially with the number of available tools

options.label: D
options.text: The agent conversation history will become too large to fit in the context window

explanation: When agents have access to tools outside their specialization, they often misuse them, leading to incorrect actions and system unreliability. The other options represent technical misconceptions - MCP servers handle concurrent requests well, costs don't scale exponentially with tool count, and tool availability doesn't directly impact context window usage.

key_concept_tested: tool_choice: auto vs any vs forced
stem: What is the key difference between tool_choice: 'auto' and tool_choice: 'any' in MCP tool configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: 'auto' allows the model to use tools or respond directly, while 'any' forces tool usage on every turn

options.label: B
options.text: 'auto' forces the model to use tools on every turn, while 'any' allows the model to respond without using tools

options.label: C
options.text: 'auto' randomly selects tools, while 'any' uses intelligent selection based on context

options.label: D
options.text: 'auto' and 'any' are functionally identical, just different naming conventions

explanation: tool_choice: 'auto' forces the model to select and use a tool on every turn, while 'any' allows the model the flexibility to either use a tool or respond directly without tool usage. The other options incorrectly describe these behaviors.

stem: Your billing dispute subagent is attempting to process refunds directly instead of escalating complex cases. It has access to get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, and escalate_to_human. What configuration change would improve reliability?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Restrict the subagent to only get_customer, lookup_order, and escalate_to_human tools

options.label: D
options.text: Use tool_choice: 'auto' to force tool usage on every interaction

explanation: Restricting the subagent's tools to exclude process_refund prevents it from making refund decisions it shouldn't handle, forcing proper escalation. Prompt instructions alone are unreliable, and tool_choice: 'auto' doesn't address the core issue of inappropriate tool access.

stem: When designing tool sets for specialized subagents, what is the benefit of providing constrained alternative tools rather than a single tool per function?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases the total number of available tools for better selection

options.label: B
options.text: It provides redundancy for reliability while maintaining specialization boundaries

options.label: C
options.text: It allows agents to choose the most appropriate tool variant for specific contexts

options.label: D
options.text: It enables graceful fallback when the primary tool fails or is unavailable

explanation: Constrained alternative tools provide fallback options when primary tools fail, improving system resilience while maintaining specialization. Simply increasing tool count doesn't improve selection, and the focus is on reliability rather than context optimization.

stem: A team lead suggests 'just use good prompting' to prevent the synthesis subagent from calling search tools instead of properly restricting its allowedTools. What is the fundamental flaw with this approach?
